title: Internal Platform & Document Portal — request/response alignment against the live-tenant probe, with remediation
method: Every row cross-references the documented wire contract in docs/folio-Master-Flows-and-Endpoints/contracts/INTERNAL_PLATFORM_FLOWS.md (itself traced to client call sites) against the actual live Power Automate response captured in the two probe transcripts committed to main. A row is ALIGNED only when the probed response's shape matches what the documented client code reads; MISALIGNED when it demonstrably does not; PARTIAL when the probe did not exercise enough of the contract to judge; BROKEN when the flow itself failed (5xx); DEAD_CODE when the flow answers correctly but no client code calls it; NOT_PROBED when the transcripts contain no result for that key. `actionable.owner` follows docs/folio-Master-Flows-and-Endpoints/contracts/ALIGNMENT_FINDINGS.md's vocabulary (that file was named REMEDIATION_PLAN.md until 2026-09-24): flow (fix belongs to the Power Automate estate), decision (two valid designs exist, a person must choose), verification-gap (the probe didn't test enough to judge), documentation (no defect, a doc is stale), or none (no action).

legend.ALIGNED: Probed response shape matches the documented contract the client reads.
legend.PARTIAL: Reachable and envelope-shaped, but the probe did not exercise enough of the documented contract (no `expect` declared, or a synthetic operation/action the real client never sends) to judge field-level alignment.
legend.MISALIGNED: Probed response demonstrably does not match what the documented client code reads — a missing field, wrong status code, wrong envelope, or a materially different shape than a sibling endpoint with the same documented contract.
legend.BROKEN: The flow was reached and answered 5xx — failed inside itself, independent of contract shape.
legend.DEAD_CODE: The flow answers correctly when probed directly, but no module in the current client codebase calls it under this operation name.
legend.NOT_PROBED: No result for this key exists in either transcript.

rows.documentedResponse: envelope.data carrying any of docs/tasks/emails/users/categories/departments/approvals — the boot call; users presence sets runtime.directory.served

findings: Request never reaches processing — trigger signature is rejected before any contract comparison is possible.
Client falls back to FETCH_ACTIVITIES per core/data-loader.js, so `users` never arrives and runtime.directory.served stays false.
Direct, live confirmation that the bootstrap-systemAdmin fail-open documented in docs/architecture/AUTH_RBAC_GUIDE.md §4.1/§9 (finding G-04) is presently open on this tenant, not merely theoretical.

steps: Regenerate the FETCH_ALL manual-trigger signature in Power Automate.
Redeploy the corrected URL into the packaged bundle's window.DGO_CONFIG.endpoints.FETCH_ALL.
Confirm the flow still returns a `users` collection per FLOW-BUILD-PLAN.md Wave 0.3.
actionable.verify: npm run verify:endpoints -- --only FETCH_ALL returns 200 with users present; then #/diagnostics shows runtime.directory.served: true in a real session.

findings: All three documented collections present, plus per-collection counts the client does not require but tolerates.

Slowest read in the run at 39.0s — well past the endpoint's 15s default client timeout budget in config/fetch-policy.config.js, though FETCH_ALL/FETCH_ACTIVITIES carry a raised 90000ms contract-level ceiling that would cover it; REFERENCE_DATA itself declares no such override, so a 39s answer against the platform's real ~15s policy would time out client-side even though the flow itself is aligned.

As a stopgap, add a raised timeoutMs override for REFERENCE_DATA in config/fetch-policy.config.js so the client doesn't abandon a request the flow would have answered.
actionable.verify: Re-probe and confirm sub-15s, or confirm the client-side override lets a 39s answer complete without erroring.

findings: DIRECT: response envelope carries two fields not in the documented standard envelope — `confidence` and `results` — on every OTP_* and portal VERIFY/VERIFY_CONFIRM response. A real, undocumented deviation across the whole OTP family.

By that shared-flow evidence, `sent` is very likely absent here too — carried as an inference, not a direct reading of this transcript entry.

rows.documentedRequest: two shapes: sign-in {operation:'verifyOtp', email, code} vs step-up {operation:'<calling feature>', requestId, otp, actor, refs, payloadDigest}
rows.documentedResponse: {ok, token|verification|proof, expiresAt, claims:{preferred_username, name, roles[]}} per IDENTITY.md

probe.why: answered

findings: DIRECT: same undocumented `confidence`/`results` envelope fields as OTP_GENERATE.

INFERRED via the portal's VERIFY_CONFIRM probe on the same physical flow, which explicitly reports `missing:['verification']`. By that shared-flow evidence, no usable proof (`token`/`verification`/`proof`) is likely returned here either.

If the inference holds, Wave 3 auth enforcement (docs/architecture/AUTH_RBAC_GUIDE.md §7) cannot function today: core/otp-identity.js#submitCode throws 'That code was not accepted' when none of token/verification/proof is present.

steps: Implement IDENTITY.md §2, less the one part of it WDL cannot do. INT-005 asks for a constant-time compare; the language has no bitwise operators, so `equals()` cannot be made constant-time and this step must not instruct anyone to try (open item 19). The protection is the lifecycle: five-minute expiry, single use, five-attempt cap, then the challenge is consumed. Then: resolve claims.roles from DGO_UserDirectory, and mint the token by whatever signing primitive the estate settles on — an HMAC is named here as the intent, and WDL provides no keyed-hash function, so the mechanism is an open decision rather than a step to follow.
Return {ok, token, expiresAt, claims:{preferred_username, name, roles}}.
actionable.verify: Re-probe with a real generated-and-entered code (not 000000); confirm token/claims.roles present. Then run npm run test:auth with AuthConfig.enabled:true in a disposable test config.

rows.documentedRequest: raw bytes, ticket in X-Upload-Ticket header
rows.documentedResponse: 401/403 expected when no ticket is presented (the pass condition — proves the ticket check is live)
findings: The flow's real definition is now known directly (supplied 2026-08-09 — not harvested, not from either probe transcript; see DOCUMENT_PORTAL_FLOWS.md §2.2–§2.3 and the flowDefinition object in DOCUMENT_PORTAL_FLOWS.json for the full action sequence).

Condition_Upload_Ticket_Missing tests only empty(trim(string(coalesce(triggerOutputs()?['headers']?['x-upload-ticket'], triggerOutputs()?['headers']?['X-Upload-Ticket'], '')))) == true — a non-empty-string check, not a validity check.

The ticket is never compared against anything SUBMISSION issued. Any caller sending any non-empty X-Upload-Ticket value gets a file written into the live SharePoint registry (https://nitdanigeria.sharepoint.com/sites/NEDMS, /NITDA_Central_Registry) — an unauthenticated write path into a production government document registry.
No size limit, no integrity check (SHA-256 or otherwise), and no association recorded between the stored file and a correspondence record.

This is known from the flow's own source definition, not from a live HTTP probe — no transcript entry exists for this key, so the verdict category stays NOT_PROBED per this report's legend even though the defect itself is now certain, not inferred.

steps: Have SUBMISSION persist each minted ticket (id, expiry, one-time-use flag, and — once available — declared file name/size/SHA-256) somewhere UPLOAD can read it back, e.g. a DGO_UploadTickets list keyed by ticket value.

In UPLOAD, replace Condition_Upload_Ticket_Missing's empty-string check with a lookup against that store: reject 403 a ticket that is absent, expired, or already redeemed, and mark it redeemed in the same operation that writes the file so it cannot be replayed.
Once SUBMISSION carries declared size/SHA-256, verify the uploaded bytes against them before returning stored:true; reject with 422 (or the existing 500 upload-processing-failed shape) on mismatch.
Write the ticket's parent referenceId and the resulting attachmentLink back onto the correspondence record — today that association exists only in the flow's own response body.
actionable.verify: Send a syntactically-valid but never-issued value in X-Upload-Ticket and confirm 403, not 200. Then confirm a ticket issued by a real SUBMISSION call succeeds exactly once, and a second UPLOAD call reusing the same ticket is rejected.
